title: Austria's Jazz Land tunnel and Brussels
summary: A band plays in a tunnel under a thousand-year-old Vienna church; the one good Brussels club is packed but noisy.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, this is the place under---
It's under a thousand year old church---

And, when the Turks had taken over that country, they had-- they made this tunnel underneath the city so they could feed the people inside -- The Turks had surrounded the city and had it locked up, and they turned that into a jazz club and this guy calls it his band - it's a steady band - he calls it his Dream Band and I must say - they're pretty damn good. Now, those guys -- that's the only professional band in Austria that I know of outside, of course, they have the big symphony orchestra there; it's a great musical city - lots of music. But, here's a little band - works steadily and when I go there I have that band each time. And, the same thing goes in Belgium; when I played Belgium, I played the only good jazz club in Belgium--

Brussels - yeah - there's only one -- really good one and big one - it holds about - oh, I'd say 400 people and the three days I was there, it was packed solid every night and people having a good time, but that's another place where the people were very noisy.
When you were playing, you mean?
